property_summary: For any caller, after calling Put(...) with some msg.value the stored Acc[msg.sender].balance is at least the sent msg.value (reference preserves cumulative balances); the mutant that sets acc.balance = block.timestamp can make stored balance unrelated and smaller than msg.value for some inputs, so the property can be violated.

After any Put by an address sending some ETH, the stored Acc[address].balance is always at least the last msg.value sent (i.e., Put never decreases the stored balance below the amount just deposited); the mutant that sets acc.balance = block.timestamp can make the stored balance smaller than the deposited amount for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any nonzero deposit amount and lockTime, after calling Put(lockTime) with msg.value = v the stored Acc[caller].balance is >= v (reference always increases balance by msg.value), whereas the mutant that sets acc.balance = block.timestamp can make stored balance < v for some combos of v and timestamp.

For any depositor and deposit value, after calling Put the reference contract records Acc[depositor].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (i.e., unlockTime is set to at least the current timestamp when Put was called if lockTime >= 0 and it's larger than previous), whereas the mutant may set acc.balance to block.timestamp but still update unlockTime the same — to distinguish, we assert that when calling Put with a very large lockTime such that block.timestamp+lockTime > previous unlockTime, the recorded unlockTime equals block.timestamp+lockTime; the mutant still updates unlockTime but because its balance semantics changed it will not preserve the invariant relating unlockTime to future Collect behavior — we instead use the observable that Put sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to block.timestamp+_lockTime when that sum exceeds previous unlockTime, which the reference always does and the mutant also does, so to create a failing case we rely on interaction with Collect: for a deposit v >= MinSum and lockTime small (so Collect condition holds later), after Put then Collect of amount v should decrease Acc[caller].balance by v in reference but mutant's balance may be unrelated — thus we assert that after Put and then Collect of the exact deposited amount, Acc[caller].balance is reduced by that amount (i.e., new balance = old balance - v); the reference satisfies this for all admissible inputs, the mutant fails for some inputs.

For any depositor, after calling Put(lockTime) with some deposit value v and then calling Collect(v) (when Collect is allowed), the stored Acc[depositor].balance decreases by exactly v (i.e., Collect transfers out v and deducts v from the stored balance); the mutant that sets acc.balance = block.timestamp in Put can cause Collect to not reduce the stored balance by v for some inputs.
After calling Put with a positive _lockTime, the stored unlockTime for the caller is at least the call timestamp (i.e. not earlier than block.timestamp), whereas the mutant can set it to a past time.
After calling Put with a nonzero _lockTime, the account's stored unlockTime is never less than the block timestamp at which Put was called (i.e., no underflow leading to past unlockTime).

After a deposit via Put with any nonzero lockTime, calling Collect for an amount <= the recorded balance and with balance >= MinSum should not trigger arithmetic underflow (i.e., Collect succeeds and reduces balance by the withdrawn amount).
